---
title: "Cutting on a Cricut"
---

This is the last mile: from a reviewed model to cut, scored and labelled cardstock. It assumes the
review and `make fix` rounds are done (see the [Guide](usage.qmd)). Commands are the ones in a
models repository that has this converter and
[papercraft-nester](https://github.com/tungufoss/papercraft-nester) as submodules; `<m>` is the
model name.

## 1. Export and plan the cuts

```sh
make cutpath MODEL=<m>    # export, then order the tool paths on each sheet as laid out in the PDF
make nest MODEL=<m>       # or: export, re-nest pieces onto your sheets, then plan the cuts
```

Both start with `make export` (short labels, cardstock fill, wider glue tabs; see
[Exporting for the Cricut](usage.qmd#exporting-for-the-cricut)). The cut planner then writes, in
`data/<m>/`:

| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `<m>-cutplan-cricut.svg` (or `<m>-nested-cutplan-cricut.svg`) | One upload: every sheet side by side, one row per cardstock colour, one group per sheet (`P04-red`) |
| `<m>-cutplan-sheets/` | One SVG per sheet, if you prefer to upload sheet by sheet |
| `<m>-cutplan.svg` | Inkscape view with one layer per pass and a hidden Review layer of the moves |
| `<m>-cutplan.csv` | Cut and travel length per sheet and pass |

Each sheet holds up to four compound paths, one per tool, in the planned order:

| Path | Design Space operation | Tool |
|---|---|---|
| `cut` | Basic Cut | Fine-point blade |
| `deboss-valley` | Deboss (or Score) | Debossing tip, valley folds |
| `score-mountain` | Score | Double scoring wheel, mountain folds |
| `draw` | Pen | Fine-point pen: glue labels and piece numbers |

The SVG sizes are in real units (inches or millimetres), so the pieces import at their real size.

## 2. Upload to Design Space

1. *New project → Upload → Upload image*, pick the Cricut SVG (or one sheet SVG) and add it to the canvas.
2. Check the size against a known piece; do not rescale.
3. Ungroup the sheet down to its paths. Set the operation of each path from the table above: Design Space
   imports everything as Basic Cut. Give `draw` a pen colour that shows on that cardstock (white on dark card).
4. Select the paths of one sheet and *Attach* them, so score and pen marks stay on their pieces and the
   sheet keeps its layout on the mat.
5. Repeat for each sheet. Sheets of the same colour go on mats of that cardstock.

Design Space changes between versions: check operation names in
[Cricut's operation guide](https://help.cricut.com/hc/en-us/articles/26922998476183-Design-Space-Selecting-Operation)
and the [upload guide](https://help.cricut.com/hc/en-us/articles/360009556313-How-to-upload-images-into-Design-Space).
Uploads are limited to 5,000 paths, which the compound paths keep well under.

## 3. Cut

*Make it*, choose the mat size (12 × 12 in for the default sheets) and the cardstock setting, and
load the tools as Design Space asks. The machine draws and scores before it cuts, so the paper is
still held when the blade goes round the pieces. Weed the pieces off the mat slowly to keep the tabs.

## 4. Assemble

- Fold first: valley folds along the debossed lines, mountain folds along the scored lines.
- Every glue edge carries a short label (usually two characters, one letter where a piece joins itself,
  longer on very large models); the other edge with the same label is its partner, on another piece or on
  the same one. Glue tab to face, one pair at a time.
- Mirror twins share a piece number: a circle for the copy on the wearer's right, a square for the wearer's left. A piece without a twin has an `A` number in a triangle.
- All numbers and labels end up on the inside of the mask (the cardstock lies good side down on the mat), so the outside stays clean.
- Wide flaps sit on seams that carry load (big pieces, horns, snout); glue them flat on the inside.
- `<m>-labels.csv` lists every label with its PDF number and pieces, if you need to check against the PDF
  instructions. The [3D viewer](usage.qmd#viewer) with *Labels: Cricut* shows where
  each label sits on the folded model.

## Recut a few pieces

A piece spoiled or cut in the wrong colour? List it in `data/<m>/recut.txt` (piece number for both twins,
`27:DB` for one twin, or a piece id like `11-01`), or click it with `make recut-select MODEL=<m>`, or
right-click it in the 3D viewer and pick *Recut this piece*. `make recut MODEL=<m>` packs only those pieces
onto fresh sheets, with the labels they already carry, and writes
`data/<m>/recut/<m>-recut-cutplan-cricut.svg` for upload.
